report:
Source review: assessed the complete meta.book.index_rows claim, both implementation associations and both associated test bodies. AnchorPages::names/table generates rows for every active name; final-component labels and full-ID title attributes provide short names/tooltips, enclosing prefix groups and page headings supply namespaces, and separate statuses(name,false/true) cells distinguish implementation and test coverage. Each linked name targets its own anchor page independently of the disclosure button; the separate hidden second row contains rendered claim text, leaving the main-row markup separate. The integration test visibly asserts exact three-anchor membership at root and namespace pages (including an anchor that is also a namespace), disclosure aria-controls, rendered strong claim text, generated individual pages, and actual TODO/N/A status badges. Its fixture genuinely invokes preprocess; captured book.rs lines 1–174 preserve fixture and recursive chapter collection dependencies. These assertions would catch missing/duplicate rows and absent rendered specification content. They do not prove browser interactions or exhaustive independent status rendering.

Deferral: spec_plan::todo::anchor_index_rows_show_rules_and_status supplies explicit TODO implementation and test entries for every-rule separate statuses and independently operable disclosure/page links. Its empty body supplies no behavior evidence. As in the independently reviewed baseline, completing this deferred portion requires browser/DOM scenarios that activate disclosure, verify rendered text and persistent main row on hiding, and follow the independent page link, with distinct implementation/test status cases. The existing TODO remains justified and visible; this review does not claim interaction behavior is complete.

Baseline verification: compared current files with the supplied historical packet, confirming exact claim, implementation metadata, test metadata, and entire spec_plan.rs. Inspected anchors.rs changes: test source now comes from matching path/Test-selector fragments and review display uses completed/unfinished output; table construction is unchanged. Inspected the changed associated integration test: it now constructs per-anchor reviews and checks Accepted, Changes requested and Unfinished output while preserving row assertions and adding status assertions. The unrelated book.rs claim-fragment migration does not change this anchor's assertions. Reassessed the historical rationale against these current inputs rather than treating the old verdict as approval.

Execution: personally ran review start, review read, exact comparisons/diff inspection, and review record; no behavioral tests or build were run by this reviewer. The coordinator separately reports 321 passing functional sage-meta tests and a passing root cargo build. Historical focused-test execution is baseline evidence only. No source edits requested.
